L01.why: Comma then 'after sunset the' with no comma after the intro phrase likely splices two clauses; but sentence could vary.

L02.why: Infinitive often leaves a fragment, but finite/participle choice depends wholly on the withheld subject and structure.

L03.why: Pure number/tense agreement; subject and time frame withheld, any could be correct.

L04.why: Period+'The' and semicolon+'the' are interchangeable; both cannot be the single key, so both are wrong.

L05.why: No comma after a likely introductory clause; but 'cools' could be transitive, so not certain.

L06.why: Comma before 'that' is almost never correct: neither a valid restrictive clause nor a proper clause join.

L07.why: Period vs semicolon differ via fixed case of next word; relative 'whose' or comma could also fit. Undecidable.

L08.why: ', that whatever' produces an ungrammatical stacked connector in nearly any sentence.

L09.why: 'whereupon' is stilted but grammatical; logic depends on withheld context, none certainly wrong.

L11.why: Modifier placement decides the subject; without the introductory modifier any subject could be required.

L12.why: who/whom depends on whether a verb follows; tense pairs also need context. Nothing decidable.
